nodes.name: Walking a BST by comparison
nodes.description: At each node go left or right by comparing with the key, recording the best candidate on the way (floor, ceil, successor, LCA).

facets.implement: Moves by comparison and handles a key equal to the node value.
facets.adapt: Derives ceil, floor, successor, predecessor and the BST LCA from one walk.

misconceptions.desc: Returned the last node visited instead of the best candidate recorded on the way.
Mishandled key == node value (ceil and floor return it; the successor must move right).
In a BST LCA, did not stop at the first node lying between the two values.

nodes.name: Deleting from a BST
nodes.description: A leaf is removed; a node with one child is replaced by it; with two children, use the inorder successor (or predecessor) and delete that instead.

facets.explain: Explains why the inorder successor keeps the ordering valid.
facets.implement: Handles all three cases, including deleting the root, by returning the new subtree root.

misconceptions.desc: With two children, lost a subtree or broke the ordering.
Did not handle deleting the root (return the new root).
Updated a local pointer instead of the parent's child link.

nodes.name: Using the sorted inorder of a BST
nodes.description: A BST's inorder is sorted: the kth smallest is the kth visit, a valid BST has strictly increasing inorder, and swapped nodes show up as inversions.

facets.recognize: Reaches for inorder whenever rank or sortedness of a BST matters.
facets.explain: Explains why the inorder of a BST is sorted.
facets.implement: Tracks the previous visited node and stops early at k.
facets.adapt: Recovers a BST with two swapped nodes and merges two BSTs.

misconceptions.desc: Collected the whole inorder into an array where stopping at k or comparing with the previous node suffices.
Did not track the previous visited node correctly (reset per call, or passed by value).
In recover BST, handled only two inversions and missed adjacent swapped nodes (one inversion).
Used <= where strictly increasing was required.

nodes.name: Validating a BST with bounds
nodes.description: Pass down the allowed (low, high) range; each node must lie strictly inside it, and narrows the range for its children.

facets.explain: Explains why every node is bounded by all its ancestors, not only its parent.
facets.implement: Passes bounds that cannot collide with real values (long long or nullable).

misconceptions.desc: Used INT_MIN / INT_MAX as bounds although nodes can hold those values.
Compared each node only with its children.

nodes.name: BST iterator with a stack
nodes.description: Keep the left spine on a stack; next() pops and pushes the left spine of the popped node's right child: O(h) space, amortized O(1).

facets.explain: Explains why each node is pushed and popped once.
facets.implement: Pushes the whole left spine after each pop.
facets.adapt: Runs a reverse iterator too, for two-sum, or two iterators to merge BSTs.

misconceptions.desc: Precomputed the whole inorder (O(n) space) instead of keeping only the spine.
After popping, pushed only the right child instead of its whole left spine.

nodes.name: Building a BST from preorder
nodes.description: Recurse with an upper bound: consume preorder values while they fit, building the left child with bound = value and the right child with the parent's bound.

facets.explain: Explains why the bound method is O(n) while repeated insertion can be O(n²).
facets.implement: Shares one index across calls and stops when the next value exceeds the bound.

misconceptions.desc: Inserted values one by one (O(n²) worst case) instead of the bound method (O(n)).
Passed the preorder index by value, so consumed values were reused.

nodes.name: Largest BST inside a binary tree
nodes.description: Each call returns (min, max, size) of its subtree; a node forms a BST if left max < value < right min, otherwise it passes up a range that invalidates ancestors.

facets.explain: Explains why one bottom-up pass is enough.
facets.implement: Returns the right triple for empty subtrees and for invalid ones.

misconceptions.desc: Did not return a range that forces ancestors to be invalid once a subtree is not a BST.
